d:
Delhi-NCR is entering its peak pollution season, with AQI crossing 300 on 2 November. With Diwali firecrackers and stubble burning expected to worsen air quality, doctors warn that even short-term exposure to high pollution levels can trigger serious health problems.
People with asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) face the risk of severe flare-ups, hospitalisation and even ICU admission. But children, the elderly and otherwise healthy adults are also vulnerable. While immediate symptoms may subside when pollution levels fall, repeated exposure can cause lasting damage.
